evidence.text: The obvious bear read of the H2-to-date pace comment — index VIX at its 2026 low, therefore a repeat of the H2 2025 collapse that got the last September print sold — is probably keyed to the wrong market parameter: the company states the Jan-May surge happened in conditions 'broadly comparable' to the prior year, making it capability rather than weather, and H2 2026 has carried record single-stock dispersion with S&P 500 pairwise correlation in the bottom 1% since 2005.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the decisive line on this name in September. On 2025-09-23 the reported half was outstanding — net income doubled, ROE 20.3%, two EUR0.10 interims declared — and the stock fell 1.51%, because the release flagged that volatility had returned to historically low levels since June and H2 activity was down on H1. Kepler's later summary of that year confirms the mechanism: 'l'annee a ete marquee par un premier semestre tres solide, suivi de conditions de marche moins favorables au second semestre'. Conversely on 2026-03-24 a +40% pace statement was NOT enough to save a print whose P&L missed. So a constructive pace comment is necessary but not sufficient, and a weak one is close to sufficient for a negative day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The visible, quotable, terminal-level statistic on volatility is the VIX, and it is at its 2026 low — 14.2 on 2026-08-14 and 14.81 at the close on 2026-09-18, down from 21.51 in early June. Anyone previewing this print off the wire copy reaches for that number and reproduces the September-2025 trade. What the VIX does not describe is the environment a relative-value arbitrageur is actually paid in: on 2026-07-09 the Cboe S&P 500 Constituent Volatility Index closed at 49.98 against a VIX of 15.84, an all-time record 34.14-point gap and the 98th percentile for VIXEQ, and as of 2026-08-14 the average 60-day pairwise correlation among S&P 500 constituents sat in the bottom 1% of observations since 2005. Low index vol produced by low correlation and high single-stock vol is the opposite regime, for this business, from the genuinely quiet summer of 2025. If the market had made this distinction the stock would not be flat-to-down through a quarter in which its own disclosed activity pace accelerated from +40% (20 March) to +70% (end May). I am sizing this at less than half of finding 1 because LESSONS.md is explicit that macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it, and no [THE COMPANY] document names dispersion; the company statement I quote covers January-May, not July-September.

A targeted search for any note, wire item or trade-press piece connecting BRP to the Section 232 exclusion returned nothing: BRP has issued no release since 18 August and its next scheduled communication is tomorrow's 09:00 EDT call. evidence.why_not_priced: Only two-to-three analysts cover the name and their numbers are visibly anchored to the guidance, not to the arithmetic: stockanalysis.com shows FY2026 consensus revenue of $966.07M last updated 2026-08-21, which backs into a Q4 revenue of $238.3M, a 5.4% sequential DECLINE from Q3, and the calendar's two Q4 EPS estimates of $0.09 are consistent with a ~$18-20M EBITDA quarter. No sell-side note, article or transcript question has laid out the implied Q4 step-down - the Q3 call transcript records that no analyst pressed management on it and management declined to forecast Q4. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be drifting -5.96% over 20 days into the print at exactly the $10 average analyst target; it would be marked up toward the $13 KeyBanc target set 2026-08-21.

evidence.why_not_priced: The qualitative warning IS on the wire - the CFO said on 2026-05-06 that FY2027 Medicaid increases 'may be lower than what we have experienced historically' and the CEO guided Medicare to +1.5-2%. If this were priced you would see a published FY2027 EBITDA estimate cut or a downgrade in the four months since the Q3 call; instead the only rated action on file is KeyBanc reiterating Buy with a $13 target on 2026-08-21 and the stock sits at the $10 average target.

evidence.text: Edge Retail Academy's US independent-jeweler panel shows the category decelerating sharply in August 2026 — gross sales +5% YoY (vs +18% in June and +10% in July), units -8%, average retail sale +14% — with the opening-price-point sterling silver / alternative metals category at -5% dollars and -19% units; August is month one of Signet's fiscal Q3 and the month the H2 guide has to be built on.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Edge series is published in jewelry trade press (JCK, InStore, Edge's own blog) five days before the print and is not carried by any financial wire, terminal or aggregator; Signet has only ~3 EPS estimates on the tape, so there is no sell-side machine converting a trade-press monthly into a Q3 comp. If it were priced, the 25-delta skew would not be -13.46 vol points (calls bid over puts) and Citi would not have opened a public 'upside 30-day catalyst watch' on 2026-09-08 expecting a raise to the top end of the range. The same series was benign through the quarter itself (+12/+18/+10 in May/Jun/Jul), so this is specifically a forward-guide signal, not a restatement of the Q2 print. Note the level is not transferable — Edge ran +12% in April while Signet comped +1.8% in Q1 — the sequential shape is the signal, and it is a ~7pt one-month deceleration.
evidence.independence: Two different sources point the same way on the value-end consumer: PROG Holdings' Q2 2026 call named jewelry as one of only two categories at Purchasing Power that failed to grow GMV year over year (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/prog-prg-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), and Pandora's calendar-Q2 2026 report showed North America like-for-like negative with US sales only 'stable' (https://wwd.com/accessories-news/jewelry/pandora-q2-results-2026-guidance-raised-early-announcement-1239092531/). The May/June/July Edge readings come from the same source cluster as this finding and are deliberately folded into it rather than filed separately.

evidence.text: The 15% Section 122 global import surcharge that underpinned Signet's 'mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year' expired 12:01am on 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same minute by Section 301 forced-labor duties of 10%–12.5% on the 60 economies covering Signet's sourcing base — a 2.5–5 point step down on India, the country Signet named as its principal tariff exposure, four days before its quarter ended and seven weeks after the FY27 guide was set.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a macro trade-law event that lands in the index, not in SIG's relative price; converting it requires knowing the specific sentence in Signet's 2026-06-02 call ('mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year') and that the guide was built on the 15% Section 122 number. With three estimates on the tape there is no published model of Signet's tariff line to revise. If it were priced you would see a tariff-relief note among the handful of SIG previews; instead the only visible preview thesis is Citi's generic 'inline Q2, raise to the top end', which is about demand, not landed cost. Slow-burning: Signet's ~$2.0bn inventory against ~$4bn COGS means post-July-24 landings mostly hit Q4/Q1 P&L, which is why I size it small.
evidence.independence: Jewelry-specific confirmation of the rates and effective date from National Jeweler (https://nationaljeweler.com/articles/15165-new-trump-tariffs-what-they-mean-for-jewelry), which puts India/China/Thailand/HK/UAE at 12.5% and Canada/Mexico/Pakistan/Sri Lanka/UK at 10% — note it disagrees with a 10% figure reported for India elsewhere, so I treat the step-down as 2.5–5 points rather than a point estimate. This finding and the refund finding below share the tariff theme but rest on different documents (a USTR action versus Signet's own disclosure); they should be collapsed to one residual if scored as a cluster.

evidence.text: Signet has filed IEEPA refund claims on most goods where it was importer of record and had received only 'a small amount' as of 2026-06-02, with management stating it is too early to quantify the amount or timing 'as well as how any proceeds may be used' — meaning the FY27 guide contains none of it, while CBP had already built out mass electronic IEEPA refunds covering ~82% of affected entries by April 2026, i.e. during Signet's Q2.
evidence.why_not_priced: The item is knowably excluded from guidance by the company's own words, and it is unquantifiable from outside — which is exactly why no estimate carries it and why the wire preview cannot contain it. The 'how any proceeds may be used' phrasing is a buyback tell: Signet has $355m remaining on the 2017 authorisation after a $50m ASR on 2026-06-08 and had $602.8m cash / ~$1.7bn liquidity at Q1, against a $3.2bn market cap. If the market were carrying this, the stock would not be at 8x the midpoint of a $9.20–$11.00 FY27 EPS guide and the put/call open interest ratio would not be 3.27. Wide band because the refund may land as a Q3 event, be excluded from adjusted EPS, or be deferred into contested CIT proceedings.
evidence.independence: The refund mechanism and its timing come from a different source entirely — Skadden's account of the post-Supreme-Court CBP refund process (https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/03/tariff-refund-mechanism-takes-shape) — and the buyback capacity from Signet's 2026-06-08 8-K item 8.01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/832988/000083298826000161/sig-20260608.htm). Shares the tariff theme with the finding above; different documents.

evidence.text: Q1 2026's headline RMB99.5m revenue (+359% YoY) was drawn largely out of a one-off pre-sale balance rather than new demand: deferred revenue and advances from customers fell from RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 to RMB104.5m at 2026-03-31, a RMB61.5m drawdown equal to 62% of the quarter's revenue, and cash plus term deposits fell RMB54.6m (RMB406.9m to RMB352.3m) against a reported net loss of only RMB19.4m - 2.8x the loss.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no sell-side model on a US$37.4m-market-cap name, no consensus estimate published, and every piece of wire copy on the quarter carried only the two lines the company led with - '+359.0% year-over-year' and 'Yiqi Aixue revenue more than quadrupled'. The Q1 earnings call had no Q&A at all (the operator recorded no questions), so the drawdown was never put to management. Had the market modelled the unwind, a stock at 0.73x its own liquid assets would not need a recurring buyback authorisation to re-rate 76%; the re-rating is being justified by the growth narrative, which is precisely the thing the deferred-revenue line qualifies. The remaining RMB104.5m balance also caps how much of this can repeat.
evidence.independence: The year-ago control comes from a DIFFERENT filing and shows the drawdown is not seasonal: in Q1 2025 deferred revenue fell only RMB40.4m to RMB36.9m, i.e. RMB3.5m or 16% of that quarter's RMB21.7m revenue, versus 62% this year, and cash plus deposits fell RMB25.9m against a LARGER net loss of RMB30.9m - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017025084635/yq-ex99_1.htm (2025-06-11). The Q4/FY2025 release shows where the balance came from - RMB40.4m at 2024-12-31 and RMB36.5m at 2025-09-30 building to RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 on pre-sales of the new consumer product: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526122709/yq-ex99_1.htm (2026-03-25) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312525313418/yq-ex99_1.htm (2025-12-10). NOTE: the RMB61.5m deferred-revenue drawdown and the RMB54.6m cash decline are two readings of the same Q1 2026 document and are filed here as one finding, not two.

evidence.text: The company dismissed Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu as its auditor effective 2026-05-27 and appointed Marcum Asia CPAs LLP for the year ending 2026-12-31 - i.e. it dropped a Big Four auditor two quarters after its revenue recognition profile changed beyond recognition, and the Q2 2026 numbers about to be released are the first reported under the new firm.
